paragraphs.text: "Healing is a matter of time, but it is sometimes also a matter of opportunity." —D'Avenant proverb
Quick and agile, Amrou Kithkin can usually escape from even the most fearsome opponents.
The clouds broke and the sun's rays burst forth; each foul beast in its turn faltered, and was gone.
D'Haren stared at the twisted lump of metal that had been a prized artifact. The fight was getting ugly.
Glory surged through her and radiance surrounded her. All things were possible with the blessing of the Divine.
Sometimes it's best to let sleeping dragons lie.
Any wall can be battered down, but at what cost?
"The day of spirits; my soul's calm retreat/ Which none disturb!" —Henry Vaughan, "Silex Scintillans"
Theodar strode the battle lines, snatching swords with his bare hands and casting them aside until all cowered before him.
The elite guard of the Mesa High Priests, the Ivory Guardians, were created to protect the innocent and faithful. Some say their actions are above the law.
And then the Archangel Anthius spoke to them, saying, "Fear shall be vanquished by the Sword of Faith."
"Foolish wizard! As you tap the power of your lofty keep, so grows my strength." —Malvern Xelionos, *Letters*
The purpose of any moat is to impede attack. Some are filled with water, some with thistles. Some are filled with things best left unseen.
A sign of battle, the Vultures circle and wait for the victorious to depart.
What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs in the afternoon, and three legs in the evening?
Few can withstand the wrath of the righteous.
"It was full of fire and smoke and light and . . . it drove between us and the Efrafans like a thousand thunderstorms with lightning." —Richard Adams, *Watership Down*
I heard their eerie howling, the wolves calling their kindred across the frozen plains.
"Visions of glory, spare my aching sight,/ Ye unborn ages, crowd not on my soul!" —Thomas Gray, *The Bard*
"Ow! Ow ow ow! Oooh, ow, OW!"
As many attackers were dazzled by the wall's beauty as were halted by its force.
The Azure Drake would be more powerful were it not so easily distracted.
"O! call back yesterday, bid time return." —William Shakespeare, *King Richard the Second*

"Full fathom five thy father lies;/ Of his bones are coral made;/ Those are pearls that were his eyes;/ Nothing of him that doth fade,/ But doth suffer a sea-change/ Into something rich and strange." —William Shakespeare, *The Tempest*
"Adopt the character of the twisting octopus, which takes on the appearance of the nearby rock. Now follow in this direction, now turn a different hue." —Theognis, *Elegies 1, 215*
Some people say that the world is round, and if you travel far enough you'll come to the other side, where everything is upside down.
"She grinned at me—a wicked grin. 'I hope you weren't relying too heavily on that, my dear.'" —Medryn Silverwand, *Diary*
Many people say that no power can bring the mountains low. Many people are fools.
". . . [A]nd gives to airy nothing/ A local habitation and a name." —William Shakespeare, *A Midsummer-Night's Dream*
". . . and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left." —Exodus, 14:22
Creatures of the Æther are notorious for neglecting their own well-being.
Nethya stiffened suddenly, head cocked as if straining to hear some distant sound, then fell lifeless to the ground.
"Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook/ or run a line round his tongue?" —*Job 40:25*

"Walls of a castle are made out of stone,/ Walls of a house out of bricks or of wood./ My walls are made out of magic alone,/ Stronger than any that ever have stood." —Chrysoberyl Earthsdaughter, *Incantations*
So confusing is the Wall's appearance that few of its victims even see it move.
Although greatly prized among falconers, the Zephyr Falcon is capricious and not easily tamed.
"'War is no picnic,' my father liked to say. But the Ants seemed to disagree." —*General Chanek Valteroth*
"Then flashed the living lightning from her eyes,/ And screams of horror rend th' affrighted skies." —Alexander Pope, *The Rape of the Lock*
The ritual of plucking out an eye to gain future sight is but a curse that enables the living to see their own deaths.
"If I must die, I will encounter darkness as a bride,/ And hug it in my arms." —William Shakespeare, *Measure for Measure*
"The highway of fear is the shortest route to defeat."
The voices of the dead ring in the heart long after they have faded from the ears.
"He knows he has a short span of life, that the day will come when he must pass through the wall of oblivion . . ." —William Faulkner
"There is no calamity greater than lavish desires./ There is no greater guilt than discontentment./ And there is no greater disaster than greed." —*Tao Tê Ching 46*

". . . [T]he ghost rides forth to the scene of battle in nightly quest of his head . . . he sometimes passes along the Hollow, like a midnight blast . . ." —Washington Irving, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
The brightness of day turned in an instant to dusk as the swarm descended upon the battlefield.
You might leave here, Chenndra, should another take your place . . . .
"High on a throne of royal state . . . insatiate to pursue vain war with heav'n." —John Milton, *Paradise Lost*
"And a horror of outer darkness after,/ And dust returneth to dust again." —Adam Lindsay Gordon, The Swimmer
"Today, for a lark, let's visit the plains. I'm sure we'll find something to entertain us."

She walks in the twilight, her steps make no sound,/ Her feet leave no tracks on the dew-covered ground./ Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—/ But those who go with her are never the same.
These days, some wizards are finding that they have a little too much spell left at the end of their mana.
Sometimes the smallest nuisance can be the greatest pain.
"'Tis now the very witching time of night,/ When churchyards yawn and hell itself breathes out/ Contagion to this world." —William Shakespeare, Hamlet
"Her lips suck forth; see, where it flies!" —Christopher Marlowe, *The Tragical History of Doctor Faustus*
"An immense river of oblivion is sweeping us away into a nameless abyss." —Ernest Renan, *Souvenirs d'Enfance et de Jeunesse*
"Black spirits and white, red spirits and gray,/ Mingle, mingle, mingle, you that mingle may." —Thomas Middleton, The Witch
"You know what I was,/ You see what I am: change me, change me!" —Randall
"In the drowsy dark cave of the mind dreams build their nest with fragments dropped from day's caravan." —Rabindranath Tagore
"For something is amiss or out of place/ When mice with wings can wear a human face." —Theodore Roethke, "The Bat"
The Walking Dead are the remains of freakish experiments by the Necromantic Lords.
Ærathi children who show promise are left to survive for a year in the wilderness. Those who return are shown the way of the Berserker.
Bogardan is a land as volatile as the creatures who live there.
"Kobolds are harmless." —Bearand the Bold, epitaph
Noted neither for their good looks nor their charm, Crimson Manticores can be fearsome allies. As dinner companions, however, they are best left alone.
The Crookshank military boasts a standing army of nearly twenty-four million, give or take twenty-two million.
Warriors of the Tsunami-nito School spend years in training to master the way of effortless effort.
"The bird of wonder dies, the maiden phoenix,/ Her ashes new-create another heir/ As great in admiration as herself." —William Shakespeare, *King Henry the Eighth*
The Frost Giants have been out in the cold a long, long time, but they have their rage to keep them warm.
"O! it is excellent/ To have a giant's strength, but it is tyrannous/ To use it like a giant." —William Shakespeare, *Measure for Measure*
On the morning of the Battle of Gal-Shan, the Sorcerer's cry rang out: "Let no bird fly, let no creature take wing, let all the battle join as one."
"The smith a mighty man is he/ With large and sinewy hands./ And the muscles of his brawny arms/ Are strong as iron bands." —Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, The Village Blacksmith
"Joining this army is easy, boy. Just survive your first battle."
"One for all, all for one; we strike first, and then you're done!" —Oath of the Kobold Musketeers
The Taskmaster knows that there is no cure for the common Kobold.
Kher Keep is unique among fortresses: impervious to aerial assault but defenseless from the ground.
The Yeti's single greatest asset is its unnerving ability to blend in with its surroundings.
The thick, moving mass from the beginning of evolution swallows and digests the animate and inanimate as it unthinkingly strives to continue its existence.
"Hi! ni! ya! Behold the man of flint, that's me!/ Four lightnings zigzag from me, strike and return." —Navajo war chant
"O Great Captain, all is lost. They tunneled, they burrowed, they trenched. They sapped the strength of our defenses." —Sorgus, *Chronicles of the Quarum Plains*
"Sometimes the bulls win, and sometimes the bears win. But the bulls have more fun." —Anonymous
"Striking silent as a dream,/ Cutting short the strangled scream . . ." —Tobrian, "Watchdragon"
"Union may be strength, but it is mere blind brute strength unless wisely directed." —Samuel Butler
An ever-moving swarm of dust engulfs and disorients anything that comes near.
The ground shuddered violently and the earth seemed to come to life. The elemental force contained in the vast wall of earth was trapped, bent to its controller's will.
At a distance, we mistook the sound for a waterfall . . .
Like so many obstacles in life, the Wall of Opposition is but an illusion, held fast by the focus and belief of the one who creates it.
"'Tis the set of sails, and not the gales,/ Which tells us the way to go." —Ella Wheeler Wilcox
Unpredictable in the extreme, these carnivorous apes will prey even upon their own kind.
These stealthy felines have survived so many battles that some believe they must possess many lives.
Harthag gave a jolly laugh as he surveyed the army before him. "Ho ho ho! Midgets! You think you can stand in my way?"
"And the unclean spirits went out, and entered the swine; and the herd ran violently . . ." —Mark 5:13
"Sometimes it is better to be swift of foot than strong of swordarm." —Elven Proverb
"Flittering, wheeling, / darting in to strike, and then / gone just as you blink." —"Dragonfly Haiku," poet unknown
"The turtle lives 'twixt plated decks/ Which practically conceal its sex./ I think it clever of the turtle/ In such a fix to be so fertile." —Ogden Nash, "The Turtle"
"Then inch by inch out of the grass rose up the head and spread hood of Nag, the big black cobra, and he was five feet long from tongue to tail." —Rudyard Kipling, *The Jungle Books*
The communal mind produces a savage strategy, yet no one could predict that this vicious crossbreed would unravel the secret of steel.
After the battle, an eerie silence gripped the forest. The losers' remains were lightly dusted with green.
"Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed unto the meek." —Ecclesiastes 3:19
"How dull it is to pause, to make an end,/ To rust unburnished, not to shine in use,/ As though to breathe were life!" —Alfred, Lord Tennyson, "Ulysses"
Leave a bowl of milk on your doorstep each night for the brownies, or they'll cause you no end of mischief.
Fierce winds ripped across the tropical landscape. What they did not destroy with their fiery breath was washed away by torrential rain.
"Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!" —William Shakespeare, *King Lear*
"Give them great meals of beef and iron and steel, they will eat like wolves and fight like devils." —William Shakespeare, *King Henry V*
". . . And at his passing, the bodies of the world's great warriors shall rise from their graves and follow him to battle." —*The Anvilonian Grimoire*
"Battles no longer served a purpose in Karakas." —Angus Mackenzie, *Diary*
He is devious and cunning, in both appearance and deed. Beware the Warbeard, for this brute bites as well as he barks!
Thundering down from Hammerheim, no foe could slow Bartel's charge.
"My power is as vast as the plains, my strength is that of mountains. Each wave that crashes upon the shore thunders like blood in my veins." —*Memoirs*
Urborg became the final resting place of many swordsmen of renown, their steel outmatched by the wiles of Gwendlyn.
Hail from Tolaria the ever changing 'Dane.
"You would never guess, at the terrifying sight of the man, that Hunding was as charming a companion as one could wish for."
Abandoning his sword to return to the lush forest of Pendelhaven, Jacques le Vert devoted his life to protecting the creatures of his homeland.
"Peace must prevail, even if the wicked must die."
Mightiest of the Cat Warriors, Jedit Ojanen forsook the forests of his tribe and took service with the Robaran Mercenaries, rising through their ranks to lead them in the battle for Efrava.
Once, the order of the Closed Fist reached throughout the Kb'Briann Highlands. Now, Jerrard alone remains to uphold their standard.
Popular indeed is the tale of how Kasimir was once a Holy man who renounced his order to take up the sword. But this tale is no more likely than any other.
"When milady was young, the sight of a rainbow would fill her soul with peace. As she grew, she learned to share her rapture with others." —*Lady Gabriella*

"I do not remember what he said to her. I remember her fiery eyes, fixed upon him for an instant. I remember a flash, and the hot breath of sudden flames made me turn away. When I looked again, Angus was gone." —A Wayfarer, on meeting Lady Orca
Livonya's own nature is a matter of mystery. Nothing is known for sure, merely rumors of unearthly stealth, and unholy alliances.
Marhault follows a strict philosophy, never letting emotions cloud his thoughts. No chance observer could imagine the rage in his heart.
We all know the legend: Pavel wanders the realms, helping those in greatest need. But is this a measure of his generosity, or of his obligation to atone?
"On the field of honor, a soldier need have no fear."
Ramirez DePietro is a most flamboyant pirate. Be careful not to believe his tall tales, especially when you ask his age.
"Political violence is a perfectly legitimate answer to the persecution handed down by dignitaries of the state."
"Remember Sir Shandlar! Remember and stand firm!" —rallying cry of the Eberyn militia
Even the brave have cause to tremble at the sight of Sivitri Scarzam. Who else has tamed Scarzam's Dragon?
Sunastian has roots in both sorcery and swordplay; he has learned never to depend too heavily on the latter.
Her given name has been lost in the mists of time. Legend says that her silent vigil will one day be ended by the one who, pure of heart and spirit, calls out that name again.
Administrator of the military state of Sheoltun, Tobias is the military right arm of the empire and the figurehead of its freedom.
"How can you accuse me of evil? Though these deeds be unsavory, no one will argue: good shall follow from them."
An explorer of the Æther, Tuknir often discovers himself in the most unusual physical realms.
A regular guest at the Royal Masquerade, Arien is the envy of the Court. She appears in a new costume every hour.
Al-abara simply laughed and lifted one finger, and the carpet carried her high out of our reach.
"A blast, an echo . . . then silence."
Nireya reached through the Gate, sensing the energies trapped beyond.
"'Tis distance lends enchantment to the view,/ And robes the mountain in its azure hue." —Thomas Campbell, "Pleasures of Hope"
"To make a prairie it takes a clover and one bee,/ One clover, and a bee,/ And revery." —Emily Dickinson
"This is the forest primeval. The murmuring pines and the hemlocks . . . / Stand like Druids of old." —Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, "Evangeline"
"Fairest Isle, all isles excelling,/ Seat of Pleasures, and of loves . . ." —John Dryden

"Resignedly beneath the sky/The melancholy waters lie./So blend the turrets and shadows there/That all seem pendulous in air,/While from a proud tower in town/Death looks gigantically down." —Edgar Allan Poe, "The City in the Sea"
